correctness.rationale: The pair-merging lemma reduces all missing length-(m+1) candidates to monotone words for roots containing an alternating (10)^m or (01)^m subsequence. Direct gap-sum inequalities yield exactly the claimed 1/2/3 missing words. Indexed-root counting is a disjoint partition; the Fibonacci morphism preserves the forbidden cyclic patterns. Checks from the actual standalone package exhaust 318 admissible ordered gap vectors, 7359 roots, 9484688 direct candidates, plus 602 Fibonacci roots; all match. Finite verification supports but does not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A natural finite-state constrained class has a complete arrangement-independent distribution of shortest absent-subsequence defects over all circular cuts. The result gives five explicit possible missing-word templates, sharp cut-by-cut multiplicities, and an exact Fibonacci-word series. This supports analytical comparison of near-universal roots in constrained coding and combinatorics on words, beyond generic word-by-word SAS enumeration.
